description: False-colour infrared satellite imagery displays a mixed landscape segmented by overlaid blue lines, likely representing Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) mapping units. Healthy vegetation appears bright red, such as the curved areas adjacent to the central river/canal, indicating agricultural fields. Buildings are rendered in light grey/white, while bare ground, sparse vegetation, and unpaved roads appear in brownish-grey tones. A river or canal runs through the centre, shown in dark blue/black. Several specific land cover features are highlighted by light blue polygon outlines. One such highlighted polygon, encompassing a cluster of buildings and associated infrastructure, is labelled "1120". This numerical code corresponds to the CORINE Land Cover (CLC) class 1120, "Discontinuous urban fabric," which is consistent with the visual representation of scattered residential areas and roads in a semi-urban or rural setting. No scale bar, compass, legend, or specific reference year is visible.
